consequence_note: The classification was reconsidered from scratch rather than inherited from stage 2, because the approved plan calls the one-time PIN reveal the highest-risk element in the slice, on three axes at once - security, accessibility and copy - and a high classification would filter every external candidate against their medium ceilings and force this stage native. It is recorded as medium for four specific reasons, not for convenience. First, recoverability is high: the subtree is additive, nothing imports it, it is not mounted until stage 4, and discarding the branch discards the stage. Second, the security axis is largely not resident in this stage - the retention property lives in the hook, was implemented at stage 2, and was proven at the stage-2 gate by a negative control that failed exactly one of seventeen tests when the sanitization was defeated; presentation consumes an already-sanitized surface. Third, the copy is not invented here: the seven action labels are human-locked and already exist in the repository, so the stage copies rather than authors them. Fourth, the two axes that genuinely need judgment - Arabic copy quality and the accessibility semantics of a transient credential display - are gated downstream on purpose, by the coordinator's own review at this gate, by the stage-5 polish loop, and by stage-7 independent verification. If any of those four had been false, this stage would have been high and would have gone native.
retained_coordinator_axes: Arabic copy review at the gate, read directly rather than taken from the report. The plan names a specific trap: an en dash renders a numeric range reversed in Arabic, and the staff PIN length is a range, so it must use a plain hyphen. This is carried into the brief and re-checked here.

reliability_escalation_rule.question_asked: Does deepseek-v4-pro now hold a material stage-specific evidence advantage, given that ox-alpha carries a transport failure recorded minutes ago on this exact stage and deepseek-v4-pro carries none?
reliability_escalation_rule.answer: Not yet. One transient stream error that the provider itself marks retryable, on a route that re-resolved live immediately afterwards, is not evidence of a reliability difference between two candidates - it is evidence that a network call failed once. Reading it as a material advantage would manufacture a separator out of a single sample, which is the same error as inventing a capability advantage.
reliability_escalation_rule.pre_committed: Recorded BEFORE attempt 2 so it cannot be rationalized afterwards: if attempt 2 also fails on transport, stage 3 routes to deepseek-v4-pro rather than retrying this route a third time. Two failures make a pattern where one makes noise, and at that point the availability_economic preference's own basis - current free / near-unlimited availability of the qualified route - is no longer confirmed for this stage. This is a routing rule, not a repair-budget rule; the milestone's repair budget is untouched either way.
reliability_escalation_rule.cost_asymmetry_acknowledged: Stage 3 is the largest writing stage in the slice, so a repeated mid-stream failure is more expensive here than elsewhere. That asymmetry is why the escalation rule is pre-committed at one further failure rather than left open-ended.

reroute.trigger: the rule pre-committed in reliability_escalation_rule BEFORE attempt 2 ran: a second transport failure routes stage 3 to deepseek-v4-pro rather than retrying a third time. Two failures make a pattern where one makes noise.
reroute.mechanism: Both failures were appended to the ox-alpha evidence record before rerouting, so the resolver saw two adverse entries post-dating the stored decision and requalified. The stage input was corrected on one honest point: confirmed_promotion_basis_candidate_ids no longer lists ox-alpha, because the availability_economic preference applies only when live preflight confirms its basis - current free / near-unlimited availability of the qualified route - still holds FOR THIS STAGE, and two consecutive mid-stream failures mean it does not. With that preference correctly out of the way, the resolver selected the registry's stable preferred general bounded implementation candidate, which this stage genuinely is.
reroute.scope_of_the_finding: Deliberately scoped to this stage, not a global expiry of the temporary preference. The route still resolves at preflight, one stage's transport trouble is not established provider-wide unavailability, and expiring the registry entry is a separate edit with its own reasoning. A recurrence on another stage would warrant that registry-level review.
reroute.not_a_capability_judgement: Nothing here says ox-alpha is less capable. It closed stages 1 and 2 of this run - one of them this slice's largest read stage - and its qualification, ceiling, constraints and flags are unchanged. The reroute is about a route that could not hold a stream open twice in a row, nothing more.

interruption_note: A host power loss occurred during this stage's parent-gate work. The implementation commit and this decision file survived; the gate record, the candidate evidence entry, this gate_outcome, the ledger advance, and verify:fast did not, and were completed on resume. No implementation was redone and no accepted stage was reopened. On the first post-restart verify:fast run the ladder went red on Biome - not on the stage, but on THIS file, which JSON.stringify had written with expanded short arrays and which, being untracked, had never passed through the pre-commit formatter. It was formatted and the ladder re-run clean. That is precisely the failure class the approved plan anticipates when it requires the deterministic checks to run last, after every durable record is written.
